mainEntity.name: How do I know if I am suitable for same-day dental implants?

acceptedAnswer.text: Suitability for same-day dental implants can only be determined through a comprehensive clinical assessment. Your dentist will evaluate your jawbone density and volume, gum health, general medical history, and any medications you take. Radiographic imaging, often a CBCT scan, is typically required. There is no reliable way to determine suitability without professional examination, so a consultation is always the recommended starting point for anyone considering this treatment.

mainEntity.name: How long do same-day dental implants last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Dental implants — whether placed on the same day or via a staged approach — are designed to be a long-term tooth replacement solution. With good oral hygiene, regular dental monitoring, and a healthy lifestyle, implants can remain functional for many years. However, individual outcomes depend on clinical factors, home care routines, and general health. No dental treatment can carry a guaranteed outcome, and regular check-ups are important to monitor implant health over time.

mainEntity.name: Is the same-day implant procedure painful?

acceptedAnswer.text: The procedure is typically carried out under local anaesthetic, meaning you should not feel pain during the placement. Some degree of discomfort, swelling, or tenderness in the days following treatment is common and generally manageable with over-the-counter pain relief as directed by your dental team. If you experience significant or prolonged pain following your procedure, you should contact your dental practice for advice.

mainEntity.name: Can same-day implants replace multiple teeth at once?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, in certain clinical situations, same-day implant techniques can be used to replace multiple missing teeth simultaneously. Full-arch solutions such as All-on-4 or All-on-6 implants are specifically designed for patients who have lost all or most of their teeth in one or both arches. These approaches require detailed assessment to determine suitability and are not appropriate for every patient presenting with multiple missing teeth.

mainEntity.name: What happens if a same-day implant fails?

acceptedAnswer.text: Implant failure, though not common, can occur. Signs may include persistent pain, implant mobility, swelling, or infection. If an implant does not integrate successfully, removal and a period of healing are typically required before re-treatment is considered. Your dental team will discuss the risk factors for implant failure with you during your consultation and explain the steps taken to reduce those risks in your individual case.

mainEntity.name: Are same-day dental implants more expensive than traditional implants?

acceptedAnswer.text: The cost of same-day dental implants varies depending on the number of implants required, the complexity of the case, the type of restoration fitted, and the clinical team involved. In some cases, same-day approaches may reduce the total number of appointments and associated costs, but this is not always the case. You should request a detailed written treatment plan and cost breakdown from your dental practice before proceeding with any implant treatment.
